newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crudes hold at firmer levels.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crudes hold at firmer levels.

text.p: December North Sea crudes looked set to hold their firmer differentials after deals at stronger levels on Tuesday and refiners still looking to buy crude to cover end month requirements, traders said.

On Tuesday active trade saw third decade December crudes gain ground - Statfjord and Forties cargoes both traded at a healthy dated Brent +35 cents, Oseberg at dated +30 cents and Ekofisk at dated Brent +26 cents.
Mediterranean refiners were seen looking at North Sea grade crudes as prices for Urals and similar grades rose and differentials were expected to hold steady to firmer.
"There are crudes left but I can't see the diffs coming off. We could see the U.S arbitrage open for crudes that will land there after the year end," another trader said.
Both Brent dates in the chains were kept and potential buyers claimed bids at January +15 cents were not accepted.
"The sellers don't want this market (dated Brent) to go up yet," one trader said.
Intermonth Brent spread concentrated on the Dec/Jan and Jan/Feb with the former trading in the low 50's and Jan/Feb betweeen 52 and 55 cents.

Up to four cargoes of Forties were heard to have traded - two in the second decade and two in the third. One - a Dec 24-26 loader moved at dated +35 cents while a cargo loading a few days later was heard to have traded at dated Brent +32 cents. The second decade cargoes were heard to have also traded around dated Brent +32 cents.
An Oseberg (Dec 15-17) moved at dated Brent +30 cents but talk of a Dec 9-11 trading ten cents lower could not be confirmed.
